evidence.note: claim: remaining_s<0 inside grace prints negative; refuted-if test passes unfixed. Ran tests/test_lease_grace_countdown.py on reverted code: FAILED 'another -'; fixed: passes
no rule touched; change confined to lease wording
commit lease countdowns; Lease.left_text used by schedule.py and reporting.py

chunk_findings.detail: `left_text` decides the wording purely from the sign of `remaining_s` and hard-codes "in its grace period" for *every* negative value, even though `Lease` has no knowledge of `grace_s`. Given a lease with `ttl_s=60`, `renewed_at=t`, `now = t + 60 + grace_s + 100` (a lease that has been dead for over a minute past the end of its grace), the method returns `"ran out 160s ago, in its grace period"`. That is factually false: `state.active_leases(now, grace_s)` no longer contains this lease, the file is claimable, and with a configured `grace_s=0` there is no grace at all, yet the text still asserts one. The previous code ("(-160s left)") was ugly but at least did not claim liveness that does not exist. In `reporting.py` the new call renders `it.lease` for an item that carries one (the shown block has no liveness predicate), so `ddflow show` on a long-expired lease now prints "(ran out Ns ago, in its grace period)" and tells the operator the opposite of the truth — the file is free. `left_text` needs the grace window (or a liveness flag) to distinguish "past TTL, still live" from "expired", and the test only ever exercises the in-grace case, so this branch is untested.

chunk_findings.detail: The test's name and the stated intent ("then ddflow next / ddflow show") promise coverage of the `show` surface, but the test never invokes `show`: it calls `left_text` directly and drives `schedule.item_blocker` in-process. The `reporting.py` edit is therefore wired only by the helper's own unit assertion; a defect in that call site (wrong argument, missed `time.time()`, formatting change) would still leave the suite green. Add an actual `run_cli(repo, "show")` (at `late`) and assert the output contains no `-` countdown and no `for another -`, so the surface claimed by the bug report is really covered.

chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_grace_countdown.py:15 (`test_plan_and_show_never_print_a_negative_countdown`)

chunk_findings.detail: The refactor replaces the fragment `for another {-N}s` with whatever `left_text` returns, but `left_text` only honours the `unit="another"` contract when `remaining_s >= 0`; on the negative path it ignores `unit` and returns a complete clause ("ran out Ns ago, in its grace period"). The caller's template `f"leased by {held.holder} {held.left_text(..., unit='another')}"` therefore produces, for exactly the scenario the bug report describes (lapse a lease past `ttl_s` but inside `grace_s`, then run `ddflow next`): `leased by a ran out 6s ago, in its grace period` instead of something like `leased by a for another 6s (grace period)`. The message that used to read `leased by a for another -6s` is still not well formed after the fix — the countdown is no longer negative, but the sentence is now ungrammatical and self-contradictory for the blocked agent ("leased by a ran out…" reads as if the lease were released, while `item_blocker` is in fact returning a conflict). The same helper in `reporting.py` is fine because that call site never passes `unit="another"`, so the defect is only visible from `ddflow next`/plan's conflict detail; the in-process assertion in the test (`assert "another -" not in why and "grace period" in why`) passes because it checks substrings only and never asserts the shape of the produced sentence, so nothing in the suite would catch it.
